title: spec(automation): a flow start input may declare that it is a record id of a named object (#29425 ruling A)
body:
domain:server#5 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmQKwKFCp1m6Pb6Q8c1

Source: ruling A on #29425 (6580257050, batch #458 item 1, maintainer 「同意」). Handled under ruling C: this card and its PR state the rule only. The ruling orders the spec half first. The server half (every start door checks a declared input) is Blocked-by this card.

**Ask.** A flow's start-input declaration gains an optional record-reference form: the input is the id of a record of a named object. The brief suggests `type: 'record'` beside `objectName`, the word the CRUD nodes already use. The spelling is this card's to set. Its describe states the rule: every door that starts the flow by name loads a declared input from the named object in the caller's own scope before the run exists. Unreadable → `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND`. Not an id → `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` naming the input. An input without the declaration keeps #29365's visible-read rule. Wire it into the flow schema and lint where start inputs are validated, with gen artifacts and docs.

Declarations: `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`. A spec **minor**, with a `Skills-docs:` line.
